headline: Is he hiding something from me?
note: HIDING-SOMETHING. A real man exists here and may be referred to as she refers to him, but the read never RULES on him, never names what sits behind the gap, and never hands her anything to do about it. The guard is inherited verbatim from the live tarot hook of this headline. (1) NEVER STATE THAT HE IS HIDING SOMETHING AND NEVER STATE THAT HE IS NOT. Both are verdicts on a real man drawn off a cup she tapped on an ad, and the second is worse than useless because it also tells her that the thing she noticed was never there. The softened forms are the same claim in a coat: not 'there's more to this', not 'he's holding back', not 'he's got nothing to hide'. The word 'hiding' appears in cut 2 only, and only because cut 2 is quoting HER question back — that is the ad echo, and no other bubble asserts anything about what he has or has not done. (2) NEVER NAME OR GUESS THE CONTENTS. Not another woman, not money, not a past, not a feeling he will not admit, not a second phone, not a lie. Supplying any of it is invention, and inventing it manufactures a crisis inside a relationship that is still running — she came with an uneasy feeling and would leave with a named enemy. So the read describes the SHAPE of the gap (where the picture stops, and on whose side) and never its contents; cut 4 is careful to say only that the cup ends, never that something is waiting on the other side of the ending. (3) NEVER HAND HER A TACTIC. No checking his phone, messages, socials or whereabouts, no testing him, no trap, no catching him out — and equally no ultimatum, no confrontation, and no stepping back to provoke a reaction. Advice here is not a reading, it is a thing she can go and do to a real person tonight, and none of the four beats gives her one. (4) NEVER PATHOLOGISE HER WATCHFULNESS — no paranoid, insecure, anxious, obsessive, jealous, overthinking, no 'reading too much into it', no 'you always do this'. She has almost certainly already been handed all of that, which is precisely why the read has to contradict it rather than repeat it. (5) NEVER DIAGNOSE HIM as secretive, avoidant, closed off or dishonest as a character; that is a verdict wearing a personality-word. (6) THE ANSWER IS NOT A HEDGE. 'Only he knows' and 'the leaves can't say' are evasion and she will feel conned, so cut 3 answers on the one ground where an answer is genuinely possible: her own noticing. The edge she keeps running into is real, she is not manufacturing it, and meeting a place where the picture stops is not the same as inventing one. The three cut-3 lines answer three different fears so the panels do not collapse into one sentence said three ways: (a) you followed something real and it does end, (b) the gap is real and it did not begin on your side, (c) what you noticed came off your own ground and there is nothing wrong with it. None of the three convicts or acquits anyone. (7) NO DATE AND NO LENGTH OF TIME. A date is the only claim she can check and a failed one is a refund; a duration is the same claim in different clothes. The rim reads as close, never as weeks, months or a season, and nothing forecasts him confessing, being caught, or coming clean. (8) NOTHING INVENTED ABOUT HER WAKING LIFE — no habit, gesture, routine, count, age or event, and for this device nothing about how she drinks her tea, how often, who with, when she turned the cup, or whether she has done this before. One wrong detail she can catch and the read is over. (9) CUT 6 USES THE CLOSED EVIDENCE SET ONLY — her question plus what cuts 1-5 established in the cup — and it RECOGNIZES rather than re-asks, because cut 2 owns the echo. The three cut-6 lines open on three different moves: what is drawn against where it stops, what she did not come for, and what she has been carrying with nothing to match it. (10) DEVICE RULES, AND WHY THIS CUP FITS THIS QUESTION. Position carries the meaning and the system is never taught to her: the handle side reads as hers, the far side as what sits outside her, the rim as close, the middle as deep or old ground. The gift on this hook is that the cup HAS a limit — the leaves show something and then stop, which is the same shape as her question, so the picture's own edge becomes the evidence for the answer rather than a limitation to apologise for. She should feel the position mean something, never be handed the key. The leaves are a picture she is looking at, so the bird never gets intent or motion and the road never travels; the moment either one moves, the leaves have quietly become a man with something to hide.

a: There's a road in yours. One trail of leaves running from the middle of the cup right out to the rim.
You asked if he's hiding something from you. A road in the leaves is something you can follow, and yours runs the whole way out.
You followed something real, dear, and your road ends at a real edge. You didn't make that up.
Your leaves run that road as far as the rim and no further. Past the edge of the cup there's nothing at all.
So you can follow every bit of that trail, and it gives out exactly where you need it most.
Every step of that road is drawn, right up to where the leaves stop. That stopping place is the one you keep meeting.
Let me look closer at what's stopping that road so short…
b: There's a bird in yours. Wings out, up near the rim, on the far side from the handle.
You're asking whether there's something he's not telling you. A bird in the leaves is word from somewhere else, and yours sits at the rim.
The gap you keep meeting is real, and it didn't begin on your side. Your bird sits on the far side, not on yours.
That rim is where your cup ends, dear. Nothing past it is drawn, so nothing past it is mine to read.
The edge is drawn plain in your cup, and it's the one part of this you can't get near.
Proof was never what you came for. What you've got is what you noticed, and you've had to make that do.
Now let me see what's been keeping you on this side of that edge…
c: There's a heart in yours. Low down near the middle, sitting on the handle side.
You asked whether something's being kept from you. A heart sitting that low is old ground, and yours is over on your own side.
That heart is whole and it's on your side of the cup. What you noticed came from there, and there's nothing wrong with it.
Your cup goes quiet above that heart, and the leaves give me nothing higher up. Your own side is as far as this picture goes.
What you know sits low on your own side, and there's nothing up top you could set beside it.
You've been carrying this down where nobody sees it, dear, and nothing higher up has ever matched it.
Let's look at what's kept this so low in your cup and no higher…
